_note: Vistas (Vistas autoload): high lookouts you walk up to and 'take in the view'. 'sights' are the areas whose place names the view puts on the area map; 'landmarks' the Landmark log ids it sights. The panorama is BinocularView.VIEWS[view], or 'panorama' (the same shape: bearings, ClimbLandscape kinds 'k', layer 'l', scale 's'). 'quiz' is the peak-finder's answer (a landmark id) and 'quiz_target' its target in the panorama. lonlat/radius_m fill in the park map (MapFog). 'pos' is in the region's own pixels: tools/discovery/find_spots.tscn with FIND_PLACE=1 fills it in near 'spot.place'. Sightlines want a naturalist's check.

vistas.title: Tunnel View
vistas.line: The whole Valley opens at once, framed like a door: granite on the left, granite on the right, and Half Dome at the far end.

targets.name: El Capitan
targets.text: The Valley's west gate. Three thousand feet of unbroken granite on the left of the view, and the first thing everyone points at.

targets.name: Clouds Rest
targets.text: The long pale ridge far up the Valley, behind and above Half Dome. It stands higher than Half Dome does.

targets.name: Half Dome
targets.text: Small and far from here, at the very end of the Valley, with its sheer face turned toward you.

targets.name: Sentinel Rock
targets.text: The narrow granite tower on the Valley's south wall, standing guard over the Merced.

targets.name: Cathedral Rocks
targets.text: The buttresses on the right of the view, with the Cathedral Spires above. Bridalveil Fall pours off their west side.

targets.name: Bridalveil Fall
targets.text: Pohono, as the Ahwahneechee called it. In the afternoon the sun behind you can hang a rainbow in its spray.

vistas.title: Glacier Point
vistas.line: Three thousand feet straight down, Curry Village is a scatter of tent roofs. Across the gap, Half Dome stands at eye level.

vistas.title: Sentinel Dome
vistas.line: A bare granite crown with the whole park turning around it: the Valley rim to the north, the Clark Range to the east, El Capitan's broad top to the west.

targets.name: El Capitan
targets.text: From up here you look across at El Capitan's broad, rounded top, not its face: the way a climber sees it at the end of the Nose.

targets.name: Yosemite Falls
targets.text: Straight across the Valley, all three drops in one line, the Upper Fall leaping from its notch.

targets.name: North Dome
targets.text: The round crown above the Royal Arches, across the Valley from Half Dome.

targets.name: Clouds Rest
targets.text: The long ridge rising behind Half Dome, the higher of the two.

targets.name: Half Dome
targets.text: Close enough from here to see the cables' line up its rounded back.

targets.name: Clark Range
targets.text: The sharp fin of the Clark Range on the southeast skyline, named for Galen Clark, the first Guardian of Yosemite.

targets.name: Mount Starr King
targets.text: A steep bald dome standing alone to the southeast, named for Thomas Starr King.

vistas.title: Taft Point
vistas.line: The rim just stops. Across the air, El Capitan's whole face is lit from the side, and the Fissures drop away at your feet.

vistas.title: Half Dome's summit
vistas.line: The top is wide and almost flat, and the edge is a long way off for a reason. Below the visor, Mirror Lake is a blue fleck in Tenaya Canyon.

targets.name: North Dome
targets.text: Across Tenaya Canyon to the northwest, the round dome over the Royal Arches.

targets.name: Mount Hoffmann
targets.text: Near the geographic center of the park, its bare summit ridge to the north.

targets.name: Mount Watkins
targets.text: Straight across Tenaya Canyon, its face falling to Mirror Lake.

targets.name: Cathedral Peak
targets.text: The spire on the far skyline to the northeast, out in the Tuolumne high country.

targets.name: Clouds Rest
targets.text: The long granite ridge right behind you, higher still, falling nearly a mile into Tenaya Canyon.

targets.name: Clark Range
targets.text: The Clark Range to the southeast, its fin of a summit sharp against the sky.

targets.name: Liberty Cap
targets.text: Below to the south, the smooth dome standing over Nevada Fall.

vistas.title: Olmsted Point
vistas.line: Glacial erratics sit on the bare granite like dropped marbles. Down Tenaya Canyon, Half Dome shows its back, the round side nobody photographs.

vistas.title: Lembert Dome
vistas.line: The whole meadow lies spread out below, the river looping through it like dropped string, and the Cathedral Range lined up along the south.

targets.name: Mount Dana
targets.text: The big red-brown peak to the east, built of old metamorphic rock, not granite.

targets.name: Mount Gibbs
targets.text: Mount Dana's neighbor to the south, the same old dark rock.

targets.name: Unicorn Peak
targets.text: The single horn on the Cathedral Range, just east of Cathedral Peak.

targets.name: Cathedral Peak
targets.text: The great spire to the southwest, the Cathedral Range's namesake. John Muir climbed it in 1869.

targets.name: Fairview Dome
targets.text: The big dome at the west end of the meadows, long clean slabs on its face.

targets.name: Pothole Dome
targets.text: The low granite hump where the meadow begins, polished by the ice.

vistas.title: Pothole Dome
vistas.line: A low granite hump at the meadow's west end, an easy walk up. From the top the meadow runs east for miles, and Lembert Dome sits at the far end like a sleeping animal.

targets.name: Lembert Dome
targets.text: At the far end of the meadow, the gentle back and steep face of a dome the glacier rode over.

targets.name: Mount Dana
targets.text: The big peak on the eastern skyline, behind Lembert Dome.

targets.name: Unicorn Peak
targets.text: The horn on the Cathedral Range.

targets.name: Cathedral Peak
targets.text: The Cathedral Range's great spire, standing over the lakes at its foot.

vistas.title: Crane Flat Fire Lookout
vistas.line: From the lookout's catwalk the forest rolls away in every direction, green and then blue. Far to the east the high peaks stand white along the crest.

targets.name: Half Dome
targets.text: Far to the east, just showing over the forest: Half Dome, seen from the back.

targets.name: Clark Range
targets.text: The Clark Range along the eastern skyline, white with snow into summer.

vistas.title: O'Shaughnessy Dam
vistas.line: On one side, a sheer drop of concrete. On the other, still water filling a valley that was once a second Yosemite, with falls pouring off its north wall.

vistas.title: Wawona Point
vistas.line: Above the big trees the forest falls away, and the whole Wawona basin lies below: the meadow, the hotel's white roofs, the South Fork winding west.

targets.name: Wawona Dome
targets.text: The granite dome over the Wawona basin, across the meadow from the big trees.
